 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice E.V.Venugopal

Order :

entities.text: Damsalapudi Venkateshwarlu vs The State Of Telangana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The present writ petition is filed by the petitioner under Article 226 of the Constitution of India for the following relief :
"...to issue a writ, order or direction, more particularly one in the nature of a Writ of Mandamus, declaring the action of the official respondents 2, 3 and 4 in failing to consider the petitioner's representation dt.06.06.2025 in respect of the agricultural land admeasuring Ac.26-15 guntas Ac.26-15 guntas in Survey Nos.111, 112,
111/1,111/2,111/ and 112/ Inaam land, situated at Rellakayalpalli Revenue Village,
Singareni Mandal, Khammam District, Telangana State as illegal, arbitrary, and violative of the principles of natural justice and against all settled principles of law and consequently to direct the respondents No.2, 3 & 4 to consider the representation dt.06.06.2025 made by the petitioner..."

2. Heard Sri Gadipe Prashanth, learned counsel for the petitioner appeared on-line and Sri L.Ravinder, learned Assistant Government Pleader appearing on behalf of learned Government Pleader for Revenue Sri K.Muralidhar Reddy and Sri E.Ramesh Chandra Goud, learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition.
3.

The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioners is owner of approximately Ac.26.15 guntas of ancestral agricultural land in Survey Nos.111, 112, 111/1,111/2,111/ and 112/,
situated at Rellakayalpalli Revenue Village, Singareni Mandal, Khammam District, Telangana.
He has been in peaceful and continuous possession and enjoyment of the said land.

The respondent authorities issued Gazette Notification No.A3/15/2025 dated 17-05- 2025 under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013,
initiating acquisition proceedings for the Seetharama Project.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The petitioner, being the original pattadar/beneficiary of the land, due to collusion between the respondents and certain private individuals namely Pati Narasallah, Pati Madhava Rao, Pati Srinivasa Rao, Pati Jhansi, Gujjarlapudi Saldulu, Nallamothu Venkateswarlu, Gurram Jaggalah, Sairi Aruna and Sairu Uma, his name was illegally removed from revenue records and replaced with those of the aforementioned individuals.
The petitioner submitted objections against any disbursement of compensation to these individuals.
(a) Aggrieved by this arbitrary and illegal action, the petitioner instituted civil suit in O.S.No.436 of 2025 seeking a perpetual injunction and correction/mutation of the revenue records.
The suit remains pending.

Despite the pendency of the civil proceedings, the respondents are moving forward with disbursing compensation to unauthorized persons, which would cause irreparable harm and undermine the Damsalapudi Venkateshwarlu vs The State Of Telangana on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56259694/
1 pending litigation.

entities.text: Damsalapudi Venkateshwarlu vs The State Of Telangana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Petitioner submitted representations and issued legal notices requesting that no compensation be released until the suit is finally adjudicated.
However, the respondents have taken no action nor provided any assurance.

The respondents' actions in disbursing compensation to unauthorized persons are arbitrary, illegal, and in violation of Articles 14 and 300A of the Constitution of India,
depriving the petitioner of his lawful property without due process of law.

(b) However, stating above, the learned counsel for the petitioner seeks liberty to file a detailed representation to the official respondents canvassing the claim of the petitioner seeking compensation.

4. The learned Assistant Government Pleader, representing the learned Government Pleader for Revenue and learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition reported no objection for the request of learned counsel for the petitioner to file a detailed representation.

5. Recording the above submissions, this Court deems it appropriate to grant liberty to the petitioner to file a detailed representation with respondent No.2, along with the relevant documents,
to claim the land in question.

Upon filing of such detailed representation, if it is found to be in order and in accordance with the prescribed norms, the official respondents shall examine and consider the same in accordance with law, duly issuing notices to all interested and affected parties and after affording them an opportunity to be heard, dispose of the matter as expeditiously as possible,
keeping in view the pendency of civil proceedings in O.S. No. 436 of 2025.
6. With the above observations, this Writ Petition is disposed of.
There shall be no order as to costs.
7. As a sequel, the miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.
_ __ E.V.VENUGOPAL, J Dated : 07-11-2025 abb Damsalapudi Venkateshwarlu vs The State Of Telangana on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56259694/
